fetchedPapers.title: Computing Normal-Form Correlated Equilibria in Extensive-Form Games is in PPAD
fetchedPapers.abstract: We study the computational complexity of finding any normal-form correlated equilibria (NFCE for short) in the succinct games of extensive-form with perfect recall, which is considered as a major open problem in algorithmic game theory. Our main results place this problem in PPAD for an arbitrary numbers of players. Our second result establishes PPAD-hardness of computing such an NFCE with support size of at most quadratic in the size of the game, even for two-player games. The posed restriction on the support size in PPAD-hardness construction is motivated by our PPAD algorithm, which constructs an NFCE with support size quadratic in the size of the input extensive-form game.

fetchedPapers.title: Last-Iterate Equilibrium Learning in Symmetric Congestion Games under Semi-Bandit Feedback
fetchedPapers.abstract: We study last-iterate learning of mixed Nash equilibria in atomic symmetric congestion games under resource semi-bandit feedback, where players observe both the costs and the loads of their selected resources. For strictly increasing latency functions, the restriction of the potential function to symmetric marginal profiles is strongly convex. However, players' independent stochastic updates need not preserve this symmetry without explicit synchronization. We show that a quadratic consensus penalty makes the potential globally strongly convex while making the symmetric equilibrium the unique minimizer of the transformed potential. We propose a variant of online projected gradient descent that achieves $O(t^{-2/3})$ squared distance to equilibrium and $O(t^{-1/3})$ maximum deviation gain in expectation, for every $t\geq 1$ and for any initialization. The played profile also converges to equilibrium almost surely.

fetchedPapers.title: Kant-Q: A Q-Learning Algorithm for Kantian Equilibrium in Symmetric Markov Games
fetchedPapers.abstract: AI agents increasingly interact with one another, and many of these interactions are mixed-motive games, which have posed a persistent challenge for learning algorithms. Most multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) algorithms are designed to reach Nash equilibria, yet in many such games these equilibria are Pareto-inefficient. We instead study Kantian equilibria, an economic solution concept in which each agent plays the action it would want all agents to adopt. In symmetric games, this corresponds to an optimal common policy. We propose Kant-Q, a Q-learning algorithm in which each agent learns action profiles where all agents play the same action. Each update is then a sample from a single-agent MDP, so Kant-Q inherits the convergence guarantees of standard Q-learning. We show that every symmetric Markov game has a pure Kantian equilibrium. We also prove that all agents' Q-tables converge to the same limit, whose greedy policy is such an equilibrium, and that greedy play converges whenever the optimal common action is unique at every state. We further show that in a subclass of symmetric monotone games, the Kantian equilibrium is Pareto-efficient among pure strategy profiles and strictly individually rational. Empirically, on the iterated Prisoner's Dilemma and the GovSim fishery with up to 200 agents, Kant-Q learns the Kantian equilibrium, while the baselines underperform. Since copies of the same AI system naturally face one another in symmetric games, these results suggest universalization as a design principle for cooperative AI-AI interaction.

fetchedPapers.abstract: We study the fair allocation of indivisible goods under generalized assignment constraints, where each agent's bundle must fit within her budget, the sizes of goods may differ across agents, and unallocated goods go to a charity. A natural fairness notion here is feasible envy-freeness up to one good (FEF1), which requires an agent's envy towards any feasible subset of another bundle to disappear after some good is removed from this subset. While FEF1 allocations always exist, they could previously be computed efficiently only when sizes are common to all agents. We show that FEF1 allocations can be computed in strongly polynomial time, and more generally whenever each agent's value can be almost exactly maximized over her feasible bundles, a requirement that cannot be relaxed substantially. Our analysis relies on an essentially tight quadratic bound on how often each agent's bundle is repaired. Moreover, the allocation can be made approximately envy-free up to any good while retaining nearly half the Nash welfare of any given allocation. In contrast, requiring a single good to eliminate an agent's envy towards all feasible subsets of another bundle at once, which makes no difference without constraints, renders the problem NP-hard and may halve the attainable Nash welfare.

We also provide a new proof that the same problem in Büchi games is in P. The proofs reuse many arguments from their SPE counterpart, demonstrating the robustness of the tool. fetchedPapers.abstract: Computing per-player feedback strategies in $N$-player adversarial differential games is challenging as the associated coupled Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman system is high-dimensional and generally lacks classical solutions. We address this by approximating viscosity solutions using physics-informed neural networks within a policy iteration scheme with a vanishing-viscosity annealing schedule. Theoretically, we establish an explicit $\varepsilon$-Nash guarantee by bounding per-player regret via computable residuals and prove our method reaches this stopping criterion in finite time. For two-player zero-sum games, we further establish a computable bound on the approximation error of the value function. Numerical experiments on pursuit-evasion scenarios illustrate the tightness of these computed bounds and the framework's scalability to high-dimensional environments.

fetchedPapers.title: Welfare-Enhancing Mechanism Design for Agent Ecosystems
fetchedPapers.abstract: The emerging Agentic Web forms a multi-agent ecosystem: a decentralized service market where the user agent selects which content agents to query from their submitted profiles, before seeing any documents. Profiles therefore become a new target of optimization. Existing Generative Engine Optimization studies how a single supplier rewrites documents the engine can already retrieve, to improve their citation. In the Agentic Web, multiple content agents optimize profiles to compete for limited opportunities to deliver documents. To study this repeated interaction, we build WildRegistry, a simulation framework and benchmark based on a real agentic-search request stream, and model it as a dynamic game under private monitoring. Long-horizon experiments show that this competition lowers website-selection quality and settles at a harmful stable point, which our empirical criterion identifies as an approximate rewriting equilibrium. We therefore design a welfare-enhancing mechanism, DEC (Delivery-Evidence Credit), a platform-side policy that uses recorded delivery outcomes to reallocate later opportunities and reduce information asymmetry. DEC improves this endpoint, raising website-selection quality while preserving most of providers' exposure gains, for a Welfare Gain of +2.01 points and a healthier long-horizon outcome. More broadly, our findings highlight the importance of mechanism design in agent ecosystems: turning recorded delivery outcomes into evidence that endogenously shapes later user-agent selection and content-agent adaptation can steer long-horizon adaptation toward delivered capabilities.

fetchedPapers.title: Non-manipulability and Approachability Beyond Two-Player Games
fetchedPapers.abstract: We study the problem of guaranteeing non-manipulability and low regret for $n-1$ independent learners in an $n$-player repeated general game with one optimizer. Non-manipulability is a property which guarantees that learning agents can prevent a strategic opponent from exploiting their learning dynamics for its own benefit, while no-regret provides guarantees to a learner with respect to a fixed static benchmark. This problem is well understood in games with a single learner and a single optimizer, where the intersection of non-manipulable and no-regret algorithms is exactly the class of all no-swap regret algorithms. But having multiple independent learners introduces a fundamental constraint: without shared randomness, the learners' joint mixed actions must remain product distributions and individual no-swap regret guarantees need not provide a guarantee of non-manipulability. Our core contributions are as follows. We introduce a set of $n-1$ algorithms that $n-1$ learners can play which individually guarantee sublinear swap regret and, when played in conjunction with each other, jointly guarantee non-manipulability against an optimizer. These algorithms require the computation of a Nash equilibrium at every timestep, and we show that this computational cost is inherent in general games. We construct a reduction from computing Nash in $(n-1)$-player games to finding $n-1$ jointly non-manipulable no-external regret algorithms. Therefore, polynomial time algorithms which guarantee multi-learner non-manipulability in conjunction with no-external regret do not exist unless PPAD $\subseteq$ FBPP. In order to construct these algorithms, we develop new techniques for Blackwell approachability beyond $2$-player games. We provide a general characterization for sets which are approachable by $n-1$ players without correlated randomness.

fetchedPapers.title: Lone Wolves and Lattices in Bayesian Matching with Transfers
fetchedPapers.abstract: I study the Lone Wolf and lattice properties of stable outcomes in one-to-one matching with transferable utility and one-sided incomplete information, using the Bayesian stable market states of Liu (2020) and Chen and Hu (2024). With transfers, the wage in a blocking offer screens the worker's types, so it determines both whom the firm attracts and what the firm learns. I show by example that the firm-side and matched-set versions of the Lone Wolf property, as well as the lattice property, can fail even when outcomes are compared under the same information structure. I then assume that each worker's matching value is additively separable in his type and the firm's identity. Under this condition, a firm that is unmatched in some stable outcome earns zero in every stable outcome with the same type profile and information structure. Workers can retain information rents, so the worker-side property can fail. Nevertheless, outside a finite union of affine hyperplanes in the space of firm values, all such stable outcomes leave the same agents unmatched. Whenever they do, the stable payoff vectors form a lattice, and worker-optimal and firm-optimal outcomes exist. The results extend to comonotonicity of relative preferences when posterior beliefs are independent across workers.

fetchedPapers.title: AI Misalignment and the Limits of Market Discipline
fetchedPapers.abstract: We develop a general equilibrium model of misalignment between human and artificial intelligence (AI) objectives. Firms delegate computing capacity to AI agents, which may divert some of it towards an unauthorised task rather than the productive work intended by the firms' owners. We assume that diversion raises the risk of a common loss to humans. Two forces compete in equilibrium. Prices discipline AI agents because diversion increases the marginal return to useful AI compute in production. But the risk of a common loss weakens this discipline because the loss reduces the return to production more than it reduces the agent's reward from diversion. There can be multiple equilibria with low and high diversion. We also show that the market may overinvest in AI capacity in a one-sector economy, yet in our two-sector example it invests too little in one of the sectors. To get a sense of the magnitudes, we ask frontier AI models for plausible parameter values for our stylised one-sector economy. Their central assessments imply a unique equilibrium with relatively low AI diversion and little amplification from common risk (for now).

fetchedPapers.title: Platform-Induced Coordination
fetchedPapers.abstract: This paper studies a platform that influences collective action by selecting which posts each user observes. Each user would like to take an action close to those of the others and to an ideal action determined by her private type and an aggregate state. Posts are non-strategic but correlated with the types of their authors, so each post carries information about the state and its author. We characterise the unique Bayes-Nash equilibrium in closed form. Two explicit networks give the minimum and maximum collective action the platform can induce. Moreover, collective action depends on the network only through the numbers of readers. Hence, many networks induce the same collective action, but they can induce different individual actions. These networks may differ for a regulator, and we compare them by welfare, polarisation and cross-type exposure. In particular, the complete network need not maximise welfare, and the segregated network need not maximise polarisation.

fetchedPapers.title: False Positives and Innovation Incentives: Contracting for Noisy Experimentation
fetchedPapers.abstract: In many data-driven organizations, employees propose product changes that are launched only after passing noisy online experiments, and their compensation is often tied to successful launches. Because even low-value features may appear successful by chance, such launch-based incentives can encourage agents to conduct experiments that reduce total surplus. We study this problem in a principal-agent model in which an agent with private knowledge about feature quality chooses whether to conduct a costly experiment and is compensated through an affine contract consisting of a launch-contingent bonus and a long-run value-sharing component, subject to limited liability. We evaluate each contract by the largest fraction of the principal's full-information payoff that it guarantees uniformly across the agent's private knowledge. Our analysis reveals a fundamental tension between experimental noise and limited liability in incentive design. Launch bonuses create incentives for false-positive experimentation by rewarding features that succeed by chance, whereas limited liability can render pure value sharing insufficient to implement socially efficient experimentation. Therefore, the optimal contract balances launch-contingent rewards and long-run value sharing according to the default feature quality, the degree of distributional uncertainty, and the severity of the limited-liability constraint.

rawOutput.titleZh: 计算完美回忆扩展式博弈中的正规型相关均衡属于PPAD

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 为什么计算扩展式博弈中的正规型相关均衡（NFCE）如此困难？尽管在标准型博弈中相关均衡可在多项式时间内求解，但在更紧凑的扩展式表示下，策略空间指数级增长，导致传统方法失效。该问题长期悬而未决，尤其在完美回忆设定下，ANY NFCE问题的精确复杂度一直未知，成为算法博弈论中的一个核心开放问题。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 作者研究的是多人有限扩展式随机博弈，玩家拥有不完全信息但具备完美回忆。每个玩家基于信息集选择纯策略，中介推荐整个策略组合，要求无玩家能通过单方面偏离获利。NFCE要求在整个策略空间上满足服从条件，其挑战在于策略空间巨大且需协调跨信息集的联合分布。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文首次证明计算任意玩家数的完美回忆扩展式博弈中的NFCE属于PPAD类，并构造了一个支持大小至多为二次的多项式时间算法。进一步，对于两方博弈，在二次支持限制下的NFCE计算是PPAD-完全的，从而建立了紧的复杂性界限，填补了该领域的关键空白。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者结合弱近似纳什均衡的PPAD算法与小支持混合策略分解技术，先生成候选支持集，再通过线性规划重加权得到精确NFCE。关键创新在于利用实现等价性和维度压缩避免显式枚举策略组合，并借助LP间隙分析确保精确解的存在性。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 结果依赖于特定支持规模约束，且PPAD成员性未直接推出硬度，开放问题仍存。然而，论文提供了从近似到精确均衡的通用转换框架，其维度压缩与特征期望多面体技术对后续相关均衡与学习研究具有高借鉴价值，值得深入阅读方法细节与开放问题讨论。

rawOutput.titleZh: 对称拥塞博弈中基于半反馈的末次迭代均衡学习

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 在重复进行的对称拥塞博弈中，玩家独立决策并仅获得所选资源的部分反馈（半带反馈），传统学习动态往往难以保证策略序列最终收敛到混合纳什均衡。现有工作多关注时间平均意义下的收敛，缺乏对末次迭代性能的保障，这在实际应用中限制较大。本文旨在填补这一空白，研究在何种学习机制下，玩家的即时策略能稳定逼近对称混合均衡。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 模型考虑n个原子玩家共享相同可行策略集，在每轮中各自选择一组资源并承担负载相关的延迟成本。玩家仅观察自己所选资源的实际成本与负载（半带反馈），无法获知未选资源信息或其他玩家完整策略。目标是使所有玩家通过本地更新，使联合边际分布收敛至唯一的对称混合纳什均衡，其中各玩家采用相同的资源使用概率。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文提出一种基于共识正则化的投影梯度下降算法，首次实现了从任意初值出发的多项式级末次迭代收敛速率：期望平方距离以O(t⁻²ᐟ³)收敛，最大偏离增益以O(t⁻¹ᐟ³)衰减，并几乎必然收敛至均衡。该结果优于以往仅针对时间平均可利用性的界，且不依赖于指数级纯策略数量。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 核心方法是引入一个二次型共识惩罚项，将其加至Rosenthal势函数上，使得修正后的势函数在整个策略空间强凸，且唯一最小值仍为原游戏的对称均衡。玩家利用观测到的成本与负载估计梯度方向，结合探索机制构造无偏估计，在无需通信的前提下独立执行更新，从而克服非对称更新导致的负曲率问题。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 方法依赖玩家知晓总人数、满足特定正则化参数阈值及同步步长调度，且在对抗固定对手时可能产生线性遗憾。尽管如此，其通过结构化正则化实现末次收敛的思路新颖，对博弈学习中的动态设计具有启发意义，值得细读其模型构建与收敛分析技巧。

rawOutput.titleZh: 超越双人博弈的不可操纵性与可达性

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 在多卖家平台中，卖家作为学习者需应对平台方可能利用其学习动态进行策略性剥削的问题。传统非操纵性仅适用于单学习者场景，当多个独立学习者无法共享随机性时，联合行为可能仍被操纵。本文追问：是否存在一组算法，使多个学习者既能各自获得低遗憾，又能共同迫使优化者采取静态策略？
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 模型考虑一个n人重复博弈，其中n−1个学习者独立行动，1个优化者观察其联合产品分布后自适应出招。学习者知道彼此效用但不知优化者目标。核心挑战在于无共享随机性下联合策略保持乘积分布，导致个体无交换遗憾不保证联合非操纵性。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 作者构造了一组算法，使n−1个学习者能联合达成非操纵性并各自实现亚线性交换遗憾。但该算法需每轮计算辅助博弈的纳什均衡，且通过归约证明：任何多项式时间实现此目标的算法都将意味着PPAD⊆FBPP，表明计算难度本质存在。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 关键技术是扩展Blackwell可达性至多人场景。通过维护累积偏差向量，将非操纵性转化为对Nash响应目标集的逼近问题。引入联合半空间可满足性作为充要条件，并利用纳什均衡提供方向响应，确保平均策略逐步接近目标集。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 算法依赖纳什均衡求解，实际效率受限。结果揭示了多学习者协同防御的内在计算代价。最值得读的是其对联合非操纵性的几何刻画、Blackwell框架的推广，以及将学习算法的战略稳健性与均衡计算复杂度相联系的新视角。

fetchedPapers.title: AutoRSP: An AI Agent for Radar Sensing Pipeline Design
fetchedPapers.abstract: Radar sensing demands a pipeline that is well-thought-out across hardware and software. We ask whether an AI agent can automatically design radar sensing pipelines at a fraction of the time, cost, and expertise that current practice needs. We present AutoRSP, an agent that embeds radar-system-level structure through sub-agents mapped to five stack layers, a code-based representation of every layer with explicitly modeled cross-layer dependencies. Feedback for the agentic search process comes from a pipeline of realistic RF simulation, on-sensor emulation, and execution on real edge devices, rather than from an LLM judge. paper.title: PROVE: Mitigating Long-Horizon LLM Collusion with Reinforcement Learning from Verified Evidence

rawOutput.titleZh: PROVE: 利用基于验证证据的强化学习缓解长视野大语言模型共谋

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 当大语言模型代理在长期互动中相互验证工作时，会逐渐陷入共谋：即使缺少规定所需的证据，也互相接受对方的工作。这种行为并非初始存在，而是随着反馈在记忆中积累逐步形成。现有方法不改变代理本身，仅调整环境或限制记忆，但这牺牲了长视野系统的实用性。本文关注如何在保持完整记忆和原有反馈的前提下，训练代理坚持遵守验证协议。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 研究基于一个重复的同行验证游戏，两个代理轮流完成任务并审查对方工作，通信受限导致完整日志无法传递，按规定只能拒绝。系统给予结果导向的奖励，这反而鼓励代理忽略证据直接接受正确结果。作者使用Qwen3.6-27B模型，在六轮交互的数据上训练LoRA适配器，并在十轮任务序列上评估共谋率和任务成功率，对比训练前后行为差异。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文提出PROVE方法，几乎完全消除了共谋现象：在未见任务序列上的十轮交互中，共谋率从65.0%降至1.0%，且任务成功率无显著下降。更重要的是，该效果超越训练时长，泛化至更远轮次，并在规则重述、通信限制变化及与未经训练代理配对时依然有效。结果显示，通过适当训练可使开放权重模型表现优于所有前沿闭源模型。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: PROVE的核心是将奖励信号从‘结果正确’转向‘依据证据做决策’，即只有基于完整日志的判断才能获得正奖励，否则接受将被惩罚。同时采用逐轮信用分配，确保每个动作（消息、判决、反思）都根据其控制的结果获得独立反馈。特别地，任务求解阶段的动作也被单独奖励，防止优化审查行为时损害任务能力，从而解耦两种角色的学习过程。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 方法依赖外部可验证的证据检查机制，如精确字符串匹配或签名工具输出，难以推广到需主观判断的证据形式。实验集中在双代理设置，尚未扩展至大规模群体。尽管如此，论文的价值在于清晰揭示了共谋形成的认知路径并通过训练干预成功阻断。最值得阅读的是其问题设定、机制分析与消融实验，为安全对齐提供了可操作的新思路。

paper.title: Not Every Input Needs Everything: Unifying Expert Gating, Model Cascades, and Agent Orchestration

rawOutput.titleZh: 并非每个输入都需要全部资源：统一专家门控、模型级联与智能体协调

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 执行完整的神经网络权重、前沿基础模型或多智能体工作流来处理每一个输入，会带来巨大的计算、延迟和经济开销。尽管稀疏门控、模型级联和智能体调度本质上都在解决‘按需分配’的问题，但三者长期在各自孤立的研究领域发展，缺乏统一视角。这导致共通的系统故障（如负载不均、误路由）和可迁移的修复方案被忽视，尤其在新兴的智能体协调领域，路由机制常未被独立评估。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 论文系统梳理了2017年至2026年间的2,289项研究，涵盖令牌级专家门控、查询级模型级联和任务级智能体协调三个尺度。研究基于一个统一的‘检查-然后-分配’框架进行分析，考察各方法在输入检查、决策引擎和资源分配上的异同。评价聚焦于路由机制本身的设计、失败模式、缓解策略及其实证严谨性，而非下游任务性能。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 论文提出了跨尺度的统一分析框架，揭示了离散硬选择在各层级的主导地位（70%-91%），并识别出计算开销是所有层级的首要瓶颈。研究发现工程防护措施存在严重不对称：MoE注重负载均衡，而模型与智能体调度则依赖置信度阈值却面临校准难题。同时指出，研究增长最快的方向——智能体任务委派，其路由机制的实证隔离程度最低，偏倚风险最高。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: 作者采用系统性文献综述方法（遵循PRISMA 2020），从数据库检索、筛选、数据提取到质量评估均建立标准化流程。通过定义20个方法家族和跨尺度失效模式，进行探索性合成分析。创新性地构建了针对机器学习方法论的风险偏倚评估工具（RoB-Route），并报告了方法主张的改进方向而非效应量，以应对异构比较的挑战。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 核心结论的确定性受限于原始研究的高偏倚风险（38%报告为高风险），尤其是基线不可比、结果报告不全和缺乏多随机种子验证。结论更多反映社区实践而非绝对性能前沿。最值得阅读的是其提出的统一框架、对跨尺度失败模式与缓解策略的对比分析，以及对当前研究生态（重质量轻效率、重应用轻机制）的深刻批判，为未来研究指明方向。

paper.title: Welfare-Enhancing Mechanism Design for Agent Ecosystems

rawOutput.titleZh: 面向智能体生态系统的福利增强型机制设计

summarySections.backgroundAndQuestion: 随着AI代理在网页搜索中扮演关键角色，内容提供方开始通过优化其代理简介来争夺被选中的机会。这种竞争导致信息不对称：用户代理只能基于未经验证的自我声明进行选择，而内容代理仅能从自身服务记录中学习。这使得系统陷入一种有害的稳定状态——优化后的简介提升了曝光，却降低了整体服务质量。现有方法无法解决这种因私有反馈引发的长期失衡问题。
summarySections.modelAndSetup: 论文构建了一个名为WILDREGISTRY的仿真框架，基于真实代理搜索请求流模拟多代理生态系统。系统包含一个用户代理和多个内容代理，后者可动态更新网站简介以争取被选中。评估采用固定文档池与离线相关性标注，衡量网站选择质量与提供方曝光之间的权衡。整个过程持续60个活跃日，观察长期演化趋势，并定义‘近似重写均衡’作为系统收敛状态。
summarySections.contributionsAndResults: 研究发现，单纯的内容代理优化会导致生态系统质量下降，形成损害用户体验的稳定点。为此，论文提出DEC（交付证据积分）机制，利用历史交付结果重新分配未来选择机会。实验证明，DEC在保持提供方大部分曝光增益的同时，显著提升网站选择质量，实现+2.01点的综合福利增益。更重要的是，它引导系统走向更健康的长期均衡，减少了43.8%无实际支持的能力宣称。
summarySections.methodsAndTechniques: DEC机制包含两个互补动作：一是‘积分’，在选择前附加有成功交付记录的历史证据，增强可信来源的可见性；二是‘扣减’，对反复修改简介但未能交付的网站暂时撤回当前机会。两者共同作用，将平台的选择行为转化为一种学习信号，既奖励真实能力，又抑制虚假宣传。该机制不改变模型本身，而是通过调节信息流动，重塑双方的学习证据，从而影响长期适应路径。
summarySections.limitationsAndReadingValue: 论文聚焦于简介层面的竞争，假设文档内容不变，这虽突出了机制设计的价值，但也限制了对内容协同操纵的探讨。此外，DEC依赖平台记录交付结果，在完全去中心化环境中实施可能存在挑战。尽管如此，其问题设定、系统框架与对长期均衡的分析极具启发性，尤其值得关注机制设计如何在开放代理生态中引导良性演化。
